title: Guadalupe, 1531
hookLine: Mary appears to Juan Diego near Mexico City and roses fill his cloak in December

cards: December, 1531, ten years after the Spanish conquered the Aztec capital. The old world of the Mexica people has been shattered: by war, by disease, by strangers who don't speak their language.
On a cold Saturday morning, an Indigenous man named Juan Diego is walking to Mass past a hill called Tepeyac, just outside what's now Mexico City. He hears singing, like birds, but more beautiful.
Then a voice calls him by name, tenderly, the way you'd call a child. At the top of the hill stands a young woman, shining.

teach.b: The story was later written down in Nahuatl, Juan Diego's own language. The woman speaks to him in Nahuatl too, not Spanish. She tells him she is the Virgin Mary, and asks him to ask the bishop for a church on that hill.
The bishop, a Spanish friar, is kind but skeptical: bring me a sign. Meanwhile Juan Diego's uncle falls deathly ill.

teach.h: THE LONG WAY AROUND THE HILL.
teach.b: Going for a priest, he takes the long way around the hill, trying to avoid her. He's embarrassed. He's failed.
And she comes down and meets him on the other path anyway. In the story she says, more or less: don't be afraid. Am I not here, I who am your mother?
She sends him to the frozen hilltop, where he finds roses blooming in December.
He gathers them in his tilma, a rough cloak woven from plant fiber, and opens it before the bishop. The roses fall to the floor.
And on the cloth is an image of her: dark-skinned, standing in front of the sun, with the moon under her feet.

teach.h: AM I NOT HERE, I WHO AM YOUR MOTHER?
teach.b: Devotees see in her face and dress a woman of his own people. That cloak hangs today in the Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City.
Historians debate the early records, and the Church doesn't require anyone to believe in any apparition.
Devotion to her runs deep: the Church honors her as patroness of the Americas, and Juan Diego was declared a saint in 2002.

how: Catholics celebrate Our Lady of Guadalupe on 12 December, when great crowds of pilgrims visit her basilica in Mexico City; Saint Juan Diego's day is 9 December.

games.q: you're Juan Diego. your uncle is dying and you need a priest. the lady said she'd wait for you on your usual path. what do you do?
o: stop and ask her for help.
take the long way around the hill to avoid her.
games.why: he takes the long way around, embarrassed, and she comes down and meets him on the other path anyway: am I not here, I who am your mother?

practice: Picture the map of the Americas, from Alaska to the tip of Chile, and let faces come one by one: a migrant on a long road, a grandmother in a village, a kid in a big city, a family you know.
If you pray, ask Our Lady of Guadalupe to be near them, the way she was near a tired man who took the long way around. If you don't pray, simply wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Guadalupe. Mary as she appeared, the story says, to Juan Diego in 1531, speaking his own language, roses in his cloak. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: she spoke his language. And she met him on the path he took to avoid her. Day eighty-three, done.
